papers.title_en: Building for the Future: A Systematic Review of the Effects of Eccentric Resistance Training on Measures of Physical Performance in Youth Athletes
papers.title_zh: 着眼未来：离心抗阻训练对青少年运动员身体表现指标影响的系统综述
papers.tldr_en: The findings of this systematic review support the inclusion of eccentric resistance training in youth athletes to improve measures of muscular strength, jump, sprint and change of direction performance.
papers.abstract_en: Background Eccentric resistance training is recognised as an effective stimulus for enhancing measures of muscular strength and power in adult populations; however, its value in youth athletes is currently not well understood. Objective The aim of this systematic review was to critically appraise the effects of eccentric resistance training on measures of physical performance (i.e. muscular strength, jump, sprint and change of direction) in youth athletes 18 years of age and under. Methods Original journal articles published between 1950 and June 2022 were retrieved from electronic search engines of PubMed, SPORTDiscus and Google Scholar’s advanced search option. papers.abstract_zh: 背景 离心抗阻训练被认为是增强成年人肌肉力量和爆发力的有效刺激手段；然而，其在青少年运动员中的价值目前尚不明确。目的 本系统综述旨在严格评估离心抗阻训练对18岁及以下青少年运动员身体表现指标（即肌肉力量、跳跃、冲刺和变向）的影响。方法 从电子搜索引擎中检索了1950年至2022年6月间发表的原始期刊文章。

papers.title_en: Clinical applications of wearable sensor-based gait analysis in athletes: a systematic review for injury prevention and rehabilitation
papers.title_zh: 可穿戴传感器步态分析在运动员中的临床应用：损伤预防与康复的系统综述
papers.journal: BMC Sports Science Medicine and Rehabilitation
papers.journal_tier: 康复医学2区/运动科学3区
papers.tldr_en: Evaluating the clinical efficacy of wearable sensor–based gait analysis for injury prevention in athletes, examining its role in rehabilitation monitoring and clinical decision-making, and identifying methodological limitations and future research priorities required for standardized clinical integration identifies key challenges.
papers.abstract_en: Gait analysis is fundamental for optimizing athletic performance and mitigating injury risks in sports medicine. While traditional laboratory assessments offer insights, the emergence of wearable sensor technology provides novel opportunities for objective, real-time gait evaluation in ecologically valid settings. This systematic review aims to (1) evaluate the clinical efficacy of wearable sensor–based gait analysis for injury prevention in athletes (2), examine its role in rehabilitation monitoring and clinical decision-making, and (3) identify methodological limitations and future research priorities required for standardized clinical integration. Adhering to PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, Web of Science, Scopus, and Embase from inception to May 31st, 2025. papers.abstract_zh: 步态分析在运动医学中对于优化运动表现和降低损伤风险至关重要。尽管传统的实验室评估提供了见解，但可穿戴传感器技术的出现为在生态有效环境中进行客观、实时步态评估提供了新机遇。本系统综述旨在 (1) 评估基于可穿戴传感器的步态分析在运动员损伤预防中的临床疗效，(2) 考察其在康复监测和临床决策中的作用，以及 (3) 识别方法学局限性和未来的研究方向。

papers.title_en: Effects of different dietary supplements combined with conditioning training on muscle strength, jump performance, sprint speed, and muscle mass in athletes: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
papers.title_zh: 不同膳食补充剂结合体能训练对运动员肌肉力量、跳跃表现、冲刺速度和肌肉质量影响的系统综述和网络荟萃分析
papers.tldr_en: Protein supplementation appears to be the most effective strategy for increasing muscular strength; β-alanine and creatine both improve jump performance, with β-alanine offering marginally superior effectiveness; and creatine is particularly beneficial for sprint speed.
papers.abstract_en: Background As dietary supplements have become integral to meeting athletes’ specialised nutritional requirements, research into their effects on performance has intensified. Yet inconsistent findings leave the efficacy of some supplements—most notably branched-chain amino acids and β-hydroxy-β-methylbutyrate (HMB)—open to debate. To clarify which products offer the greatest benefit, we undertook a systematic review and network meta-analysis aimed at identifying the supplements most effective for athletes, including protein, creatine, β-alanine, HMB, vitamin D, caffeine, and others. Methods PubMed, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, Embase and SPORTDiscus were searched from database inception to 15 March 2024 for RCTs evaluating the effects of dietary supplements (including but not limited to protein, creatine, β-alanine, HMB, caffeine, and vitamin D) on athletic performance. papers.abstract_zh: 背景 随着膳食补充剂成为满足运动员特殊营养需求不可或缺的一部分，对其性能影响的研究也随之加剧。然而，不一致的研究结果使得某些补充剂（尤其是支链氨基酸和β-羟基-β-甲基丁酸 (HMB)）的功效仍存在争议。为了阐明哪些产品能提供最大益处，我们进行了一项系统综述和网络荟萃分析，旨在确定对运动员最有效的补充剂，包括蛋白质、肌酸、β-丙氨酸、HMB、维生素D、咖啡因等。方法...

papers.title_en: The Biomechanical Influence of Step Width on Typical Locomotor Activities: A Systematic Review
papers.title_zh: 步宽对典型运动活动生物力学影响的系统综述
papers.tldr_en: A systematic review of published findings to determine the influence of acute changes in step width on locomotion biomechanics and provide implications for injury prevention and enhanced sports performance found that increasing step width may be beneficial for specific injury rehabilitation.
papers.abstract_en: Step width is a spatial variable in the frontal plane, defined as the mediolateral distance between the heel (forefoot during sprinting) of bilateral feet at initial contact. Variations in step width may impact the lower limb biomechanics. This systematic review aimed to synthesize the published findings to determine the influence of acute changes in step width on locomotion biomechanics and provide implications for injury prevention and enhanced sports performance. Literature was identified, selected, and appraised in accordance with the methods of a systematic review. Four electronic databases (Web of Science, MEDLINE via PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect) were searched up until May 2023 with the development of inclusion criteria based on the PICO model. papers.title_en: Writing High-Quality Case Studies in Sport Science.
papers.title_zh: 运动科学中高质量案例研究的撰写
papers.journal: International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance
papers.abstract_en:
PURPOSE
Sport-physiology and -performance research often relies on group designs that compare experimental and control groups and/or preintervention and postintervention results. This commentary highlights the key elements of a high-quality case study and provides clear guidelines for readers and authors of the International Journal of Sports Physiology and Performance. We propose 4 essential components. First, case studies should offer relevant and original insights by tackling novel issues and defining a clear purpose. Second, they must employ rigorous methodology, encompassing careful participant selection, comprehensive data collection from diverse sources (eg, interviews, surveys, physiological tests, training diaries, competition data), and deliberate data analysis that explicitly addresses factors influencing performance changes. papers.title_en: Impact of Neural network-quantified musical groove on cyclists’ joint coordination and muscle synergy: a repeated measures study
papers.title_zh: 神经网络量化音乐律动对骑自行车者关节协调和肌肉协同的影响：一项重复测量研究
papers.journal_tier: 康复医学1区/工程：生物医学2区/神经科学2区 TOP
papers.tldr_en: High-groove music promotes more coordinated movement patterns during cycling through two key mechanisms: optimized joint coordination, particularly in proximal–distal (hip-ankle) and axial (pelvis-torso) linkages, and reorganization of neuromuscular control strategies evidenced by increased synergy complexity and selective activation of postural stabilizers (SOL).
papers.abstract_en: While music is known to influence exercise performance through auditory-motor coupling, the biomechanical mechanisms by which musical groove—characterized by rhythmic drive and movement-inducing qualities—modulates cycling coordination remain poorly understood. This study investigates how groove levels systematically alter lower extremity kinematics and neuromuscular control during high-torque cycling. Twenty-four well-trained, right-handed cyclists completed high-torque cycling trials under three counterbalanced conditions: metronome (control), low-groove (LG), and high-groove (HG) music, with groove levels objectively classified by a validated deep learning model (R2 = 0.85).
